rationale: At depth 2, below the limit 6, four reusable obligations provide a useful split: presentation independence, semilinear invariance after base change, invertibility of compatible coaction twists, and descent of tensor-ideal membership. Only the second depends on the first. The parent constructs its finite presentation, transports the twist across (A⊗H)⊗_A M ≅ M⊗H, and applies these children followed by its existing coideal-dichotomy and determinantal-projectivity prerequisites. Those existing nodes are not duplicated.

subproblems.title: Presentation independence of determinantal ideals
subproblems.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module whose additive group is commutative. Let n,p,n′,p′ be natural numbers, P an n-by-p matrix and Q an n′-by-p′ matrix over R, and let π:R^n→M and π′:R^{n′}→M be surjective R-linear maps with ker(π)=im(P) and ker(π′)=im(Q). For every natural number r, the ideal generated by the (n−r)-minors of P equals the ideal generated by the (n′−r)-minors of Q. Subtraction is truncated at zero; minors use injective row and column selections, the empty determinant is 1, and an unavailable positive size generates the zero ideal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n p n' p' : ℕ) (P : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin p) R) (Q : Matrix (Fin n') (Fin p') R) (π : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (π' : (Fin n' → R) →ₗ[R] M) (_hπ : Function.Surjective π) (_hker : LinearMap.ker π = LinearMap.range P.mulVecLin) (_hπ' : Function.Surjective π') (_hker' : LinearMap.ker π' = LinearMap.range Q.mulVecLin) (r : ℕ), (Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin (n - r) ↪ Fin n) (cols : Fin (n - r) ↪ Fin p), x = Matrix.det (P.submatrix rows cols)}) = Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin (n' - r) ↪ Fin n') (cols : Fin (n' - r) ↪ Fin p'), x = Matrix.det (Q.submatrix rows cols)}
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. For a finite matrix B write D_s(B) for the ideal generated by its s-by-s minors with injective row and column selections. In particular D_0(B)=R, since both selections from the empty set exist and the empty determinant is 1. If the size is unavailable, the generating set is empty and its ideal is zero.
2. Suppose the columns of B are linear combinations of the columns of C, with the same row set. For any selected s rows and s columns of B, expand the determinant multilinearly in its columns. Each term is a coefficient times the determinant of s selected columns of C on those rows. If any columns repeat, alternation makes the determinant zero; otherwise those columns constitute an injective selection and give a generator of D_s(C). Thus D_s(B)⊆D_s(C). For s=0 both ideals are R. Consequently two finite column lists generating the same submodule give equal ideals. The identical expansion in rows shows D_s(UB)⊆D_s(B) for any compatible square matrix U; when U is invertible, applying the inclusion to U⁻¹ proves equality. The column argument proves invariance under invertible column operations as well.
3. Expanding an (s+1)-minor along one row writes it as a sum of entries times s-minors. Hence D_(s+1)(B)⊆D_s(B), including s=0. If there are no (s+1)-minors the inclusion is automatic.
4. Let m_1,…,m_N generate M and let B be a finite matrix whose columns generate all their relations. Adjoin a redundant generator y=Σ_i a_i m_i. The new relation module is generated by the old columns with last coordinate zero and by v=(−a_1,…,−a_N,1): for any relation (b,c), subtract c v, leaving the old relation (b+c a,0). The resulting relation matrix is [[B,−a],[0,1]]. Adding a_i times its last row to row i transforms it into diag(B,1); this row transformation is invertible, with inverse obtained by subtraction.
5. Fix r<N and put s=N−r≥1. In diag(B,1), an (s+1)-minor using both the new row and new column is, up to sign, an s-minor of B, and every s-minor occurs this way. A minor using exactly one of the new row and new column has a zero row or column. A minor using neither is an (s+1)-minor of B and belongs to D_s(B) by step 3. These statements, together with step 2, prove that adjoining y preserves D_(N−r)(B), with the size increased to (N+1)−r in the new presentation. For r=N the old size is zero and the new 1-minors include 1. For r>N both truncated sizes are zero. Thus adjoining a redundant generator preserves the ideal for every r, including N=0.
6. For the supplied presentation π, take the generators π(e_i) and relation columns P; the kernel hypothesis says precisely that these are all the relations. Do the same for π′ and Q. Adjoin the generators from π′ to the first list and those from π to the second list. Surjectivity expresses each added generator as a linear combination of the original list, so repeated application of steps 4–5 is valid. The two enlarged lists differ only by a permutation. Permuting the corresponding coordinates is an invertible row operation. After this permutation the two finite relation lists generate the same kernel, so step 2 equates their minor ideals. Undoing the equalities from the redundant-generator additions proves the claimed equality for the original presentations and the given r.
proof_key_steps: Establish minor-ideal containment by multilinear column and row expansion.
Derive invariance under changing relation generators and invertible row operations.
Use cofactor expansion to compare consecutive minor sizes.
Describe the kernel after adding a redundant module generator and reduce its matrix to diag(B,1).
Check all truncated-size cases and compare the two presentations through their combined generating list.

subproblems.title: Semilinear invariance of extended presentation ideals
subproblems.statement: Let R and S be commutative rings with a specified R-algebra structure on S, and write φ:R→S for its structure map. Let M be an R-module with commutative additive group. Let n,p be natural numbers, P an n-by-p matrix over R, and π:R^n→M a surjective R-linear map with ker(π)=im(P). Put L=S⊗_R M, with S acting on its first tensor factor. Let θ:S→S be a ring automorphism and T:L→L an additive bijection satisfying T(sx)=θ(s)T(x) for every s∈S and x∈L. For each natural number r, let J be the ideal generated by the (n−r)-minors of P, with truncated subtraction and the empty-minor convention. Then θ maps the extended ideal JS onto itself.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (n p : ℕ) (P : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin p) R) (π : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] M) (_hπ : Function.Surjective π) (_hker : LinearMap.ker π = LinearMap.range P.mulVecLin) (θ : S ≃+* S) (T : TensorProduct R S M ≃+ TensorProduct R S M) (_hT : ∀ (s : S) (x : TensorProduct R S M), T (s • x) = θ s • T x) (r : ℕ), let J : Ideal R := Ideal.span {x : R | ∃ (rows : Fin (n - r) ↪ Fin n) (cols : Fin (n - r) ↪ Fin p), x = Matrix.det (P.submatrix rows cols)}; Ideal.map θ.toRingHom (Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) J) = Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) J
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Fix r and write φ for the algebra map. Put m_i=π(e_i), L=S⊗_R M, and P_S=φ(P) entrywise. Define q:S^n→L by q(b)=Σ_i b_i·(1⊗m_i). It is S-linear. It is surjective because, for any pure tensor s⊗m, surjectivity of π writes m=Σ_i a_i m_i, giving s⊗m=Σ_i sφ(a_i)·(1⊗m_i); finite sums of pure tensors exhaust L. Every column of P_S is killed by q because the corresponding column of P is killed by π.
2. Let C=S^n/im(P_S). The map q descends to an S-linear map α:C→L. The R-linear map x↦[φ(x)] from R^n to C kills im(P): if x=P y, then φ(x)=P_S φ(y). Since ker(π)=im(P) and π is surjective, it induces an R-linear map β:M→C with β(m_i)=[e_i], where C is viewed as an R-module through φ. The balanced map (s,m)↦sβ(m) induces an S-linear map β̂:L→C. On each [e_i], β̂α is the identity, and on each s⊗m_i, αβ̂ is the identity. These elements generate C and L respectively, so α and β̂ are inverse. It follows that ker(q)=im(P_S).
3. Write I=D_(n−r)(P_S). The determinant permutation formula gives det(φ(B))=φ(det(B)) for every square submatrix B. The row and column selections have unchanged index sets under entrywise application of φ. The ideal generated by their image determinants is exactly Ideal.map φ J, so I=JS. This also covers size zero, where the determinant is 1, and unavailable sizes, where both generating sets are empty.
4. Apply θ⁻¹ entrywise to coefficient vectors and define q_θ(b)=T(q(θ⁻¹(b))). This is additive. For s∈S, the assumed semilinearity gives q_θ(sb)=T(θ⁻¹(s)q(θ⁻¹(b)))=s q_θ(b), so q_θ is S-linear. It is surjective because each of the three maps defining it is surjective.
5. Let P_θ=θ(P_S) entrywise. Injectivity of T shows q_θ(b)=0 exactly when θ⁻¹(b) lies in im(P_S). This is equivalent to b lying in im(P_θ): apply θ to an equation θ⁻¹(b)=P_S c to obtain b=P_θ θ(c), and apply θ⁻¹ for the converse. Thus ker(q_θ)=im(P_θ).
6. Apply the sibling theorem p05_fr_rhm_presentation_ideals_eq_a5b449214a over S to the two presentations (P_S,q) and (P_θ,q_θ), with the same n,p,r. It yields D_(n−r)(P_θ)=D_(n−r)(P_S). The determinant formula again identifies the left-hand ideal with Ideal.map θ I. Substituting I=Ideal.map φ J proves the exact asserted equality.
proof_key_steps: Construct the base-changed presentation and prove its exactness using mutually inverse cokernel and tensor maps.
Identify its determinantal ideal with the extension of the original ideal.
Transport the presentation through the semilinear additive bijection.
Apply presentation independence and the determinant ring-map identity.

subproblems.title: Invertible compatible coaction twists on tensor products
subproblems.statement: Let k be a field, A and H commutative Hopf k-algebras, and ι:A→H a k-bialgebra homomorphism. Let M be an additive commutative group with k-module and A-module structures satisfying (c·a)·m=c·(a·m). Write S=A⊗_k H and W=M⊗_k H. Suppose W is supplied with an S-module structure satisfying (a⊗h)·(m⊗g)=(a·m)⊗hg for all a,h,m,g. Let μ:M→W be k-linear, coassociative after the tensor associator, and counital after W→M⊗k≅M. Assume μ(a·m)=Σ a_1·m_0⊗ι(a_2)m_1; precisely, the sum over the fixed Coalgebra.Repr.arbitrary representation of Δ_A(a) is the tensor-map formula in the Lean statement. Then there exist a k-algebra automorphism θ of S and a k-linear automorphism T of W such that θ(a⊗h)=(id_A⊗ι)(Δ_A(a))(1⊗h), T(m⊗h)=(id_M⊗(h·−))(μ(m)), and T(s·x)=θ(s)·T(x) for all s∈S and x∈W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {k : Type*} [Field k] {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [HopfAlgebra k A] {H : Type*} [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra k H] (ι : BialgHom k A H) {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower k A M] [Module (TensorProduct k A H) (TensorProduct k M H)] (_hact : ∀ (a : A) (h : H) (m : M) (g : H), (TensorProduct.tmul k a h) • (TensorProduct.tmul k m g) = TensorProduct.tmul k (a • m) (h * g)) (μ : M →ₗ[k] TensorProduct k M H) (_hcoassoc : ∀ m : M, TensorProduct.assoc k M H H ((TensorProduct.map μ (LinearMap.id : H →ₗ[k] H)) (μ m)) = (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[k] M) (Coalgebra.comul (R := k))) (μ m)) (_hcounit : ∀ m : M, TensorProduct.rid k M ((TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[k] M) (Coalgebra.counit (R := k))) (μ m)) = m) (_hcompat : ∀ (a : A) (m : M), let d := Coalgebra.Repr.arbitrary k a; μ (a • m) = ∑ i ∈ d.index, TensorProduct.map ((Algebra.lsmul k k M) (d.left i)) (LinearMap.mulLeft k (ι (d.right i))) (μ m)), ∃ (θ : TensorProduct k A H ≃ₐ[k] TensorProduct k A H) (T : TensorProduct k M H ≃ₗ[k] TensorProduct k M H), (∀ (a : A) (h : H), θ (TensorProduct.tmul k a h) = (TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : A →ₗ[k] A) ι.toLinearMap) (Coalgebra.comul (R := k) a) * TensorProduct.tmul k (1 : A) h) ∧ (∀ (m : M) (h : H), T (TensorProduct.tmul k m h) = TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[k] M) (LinearMap.mulLeft k h) (μ m)) ∧ (∀ (s : TensorProduct k A H) (x : TensorProduct k M H), T (s • x) = θ s • T x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. All tensor products below are over k. Write Δ_A(a)=Σa_1⊗a_2 and μ(m)=Σm_0⊗m_1. Expressions using these finite sums are representation-independent: each is obtained from the tensor itself by composing linear maps induced by the displayed bilinear multiplications or actions. In particular, the given Coalgebra.Repr.arbitrary compatibility becomes the stated Sweedler formula.
2. Define k-linear maps θ_0,ψ:S→S on pure tensors by θ_0(a⊗h)=Σa_1⊗ι(a_2)h and ψ(a⊗h)=Σa_1⊗ι(S_A(a_2))h. Each prescription is k-bilinear in a,h, so the tensor universal property gives the claimed maps. Multiplicativity of Δ_A and ι gives θ_0((a⊗h)(b⊗g))=Σa_1b_1⊗ι(a_2b_2)hg=θ_0(a⊗h)θ_0(b⊗g). Bilinearity extends this equality to arbitrary tensors. Also θ_0(1⊗1)=1⊗1, and k-linearity then shows that θ_0 preserves the embedded k-scalars.
3. By coassociativity, θ_0ψ(a⊗h)=Σa_1⊗ι(a_2 S_A(a_3))h and ψθ_0(a⊗h)=Σa_1⊗ι(S_A(a_2)a_3)h. In the first expression apply the antipode identity multiplying the last two factors in the order id⊗S; in the second use S⊗id. Each expression becomes Σa_1⊗ε_A(a_2)h=a⊗h by counitality and k-balancing. The equalities hold on all tensors by linearity. Thus ψ is a two-sided inverse to θ_0, and θ_0 defines the required k-algebra automorphism θ. Its asserted formula is exactly its definition, using tensor-product multiplication.
4. Define k-linear maps T_0,U:W→W on pure tensors by T_0(m⊗h)=Σm_0⊗m_1h and U(m⊗h)=Σm_0⊗S_H(m_1)h. Both prescriptions are k-bilinear in m,h, since μ and the antipode are k-linear and multiplication is bilinear, so both descend to the tensor product.
5. Coassociativity of μ rewrites T_0U(m⊗h) as Σm_0⊗m_1S_H(m_2)h, and UT_0(m⊗h) as Σm_0⊗S_H(m_1)m_2h. The two antipode identities reduce these to Σm_0⊗ε_H(m_1)h. The assumed counitality of μ and k-balancing identify this with m⊗h. Hence T_0 and U are mutually inverse on pure tensors and therefore everywhere. They define a k-linear automorphism T. Since H is commutative, m_1h=hm_1, which is precisely the pure-tensor formula for T demanded in the statement.
6. For a∈A, h,g∈H and m∈M, the supplied S-action and compatibility of μ give T((a⊗h)·(m⊗g))=Σa_1·m_0⊗ι(a_2)m_1hg. On the other hand θ(a⊗h)·T(m⊗g)=Σa_1·m_0⊗(ι(a_2)h)(m_1g), using the same supplied action on each pure tensor. Commutativity and associativity in H equate these expressions. Both sides are additive separately in the scalar tensor and the module tensor; expressing arbitrary tensors as finite sums of pure tensors therefore proves T(s·x)=θ(s)·T(x) for all s,x. Together with steps 3 and 5, this proves every part of the existential conclusion.
proof_key_steps: Interpret the compatibility formula through the tensor universal property.
Construct the algebra twist and its inverse using Δ_A and S_A.
Use antipode and counit identities to prove the algebra twist invertible.
Construct the coaction twist and its inverse using μ and S_H.
Use coassociativity and counitality to prove the module twist invertible.
Check semilinearity on pure tensors and extend by additivity.

subproblems.title: Descent of extended-ideal membership through an injective tensor map
subproblems.statement: Let k be a field, A and H commutative k-algebras, f:A→H an injective k-linear map, J an ideal of A, and t∈A⊗_k A. Extend J to A⊗_k H along the algebra homomorphism a↦a⊗1. If (id_A⊗f)(t) belongs to this extended ideal, then t belongs to the k-linear span of all a⊗b with a∈J and b∈A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {k : Type*} [Field k] {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] {H : Type*} [CommRing H] [Algebra k H] (f : A →ₗ[k] H) (_hf : Function.Injective f) (J : Ideal A) (t : TensorProduct k A A) (_ht : TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : A →ₗ[k] A) f t ∈ Ideal.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : A →ₐ[k] TensorProduct k A H).toRingHom J), t ∈ Submodule.span k {z : TensorProduct k A A | ∃ a ∈ J, ∃ b : A, z = TensorProduct.tmul k a b}
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Let E_H be the k-linear span in A⊗_k H of tensors j⊗h with j∈J. It is an ideal of A⊗_k H: multiplying a generating tensor j⊗h by a pure tensor a⊗g gives aj⊗gh, whose first factor lies in J. Distributing over finite sums of pure tensors and over the linear combinations defining the span proves closure under multiplication by every element. Its additive closure and zero follow from its definition as a submodule.
2. The ideal E_H contains every j⊗1, so it contains the extension of J along a↦a⊗1. Conversely, each j⊗h=(j⊗1)(1⊗h) belongs to that extended ideal. An ideal in a k-algebra is closed under k-scalar multiplication because scalar multiplication is multiplication by the image of the scalar. Therefore the extended ideal contains their k-linear span E_H. The two are equal, so the hypothesis places (id_A⊗f)(t) in E_H.
3. Choose a k-basis of A. Injectivity of f makes its image a linearly independent subset of H. Extend that image to a basis of H, define λ on the image basis by λ(f(a_i))=a_i and on the added basis vectors by zero, and extend k-linearly. This constructs λ:H→A with λ∘f=id_A.
4. Put E_A=span_k{j⊗a:j∈J,a∈A}. The linear map id_A⊗λ carries E_H into E_A, because it sends each generating j⊗h to j⊗λ(h). Its composite with id_A⊗f is the identity on A⊗_k A: check this on a⊗b using λ(f(b))=b, then extend linearly. Applying id_A⊗λ to the membership from step 2 therefore gives t∈E_A, exactly the conclusion.
proof_key_steps: Identify the extended ideal with the span of tensors whose first factor lies in J.
Construct a linear retraction of the injective map f by extending a basis.
Apply id⊗λ to descend membership to the corresponding span in A⊗A.
